ozocerite.m: A waxy mineral that is a mixture of hydrocarbons and occurs in association with petroleum; some varieties are used in making ceresin and candles.

ozone.m: A colourless gas (O3) soluble in alkalis and cold water; a strong oxidising agent; can be produced by electric discharge in oxygen or by the action of ultraviolet radiation on oxygen in the stratosphere (where it acts as a screen for ultraviolet radiation).

ozonide.m: Any of a class of unstable chemical compounds resulting from the addition of ozone to a double bond in an unsaturated compound.

ozonides.m: Any of a class of unstable chemical compounds resulting from the addition of ozone to a double bond in an unsaturated compound.

ozonosphere.m: A layer in the stratosphere (at approximately 20 miles) that contains a concentration of ozone sufficient to block most ultraviolet radiation from the sun.
